title: Design Linked List Operations
hints: first, how would you parse each token into an operation name and its numeric arguments, given they're joined by underscores?
addAtHead and addAtTail are just addAtIndex with index 0 or index length - can you implement one general insert-at-index helper?
carefully define what 'invalid index' means for each operation (get and deleteAtIndex need a strictly-in-range index, addAtIndex additionally allows index == length)
walk the tokens in order, mutate your working list according to the operation, and whenever you see a get, append its result to your answer list
commonMistakes: allowing addAtIndex to succeed when index > length, when it should be ignored
off-by-one errors distinguishing 'index == length is valid for addAtIndex' from 'index == length is invalid for get and deleteAtIndex'
mis-parsing tokens when splitting on underscore, especially forgetting addAtIndex has two numeric parts

content.problemStatement:
Simulate a singly linked list that starts empty and supports these
operations, given as a single space-delimited string ops where each
operation is one token (values within a token are joined by
underscores, since the whole string is split on spaces):

- "addAtHead_v": insert a new node with value v at the head of the list.
- "addAtTail_v": insert a new node with value v at the tail of the list.
- "addAtIndex_i_v": insert a new node with value v so that it becomes
  the node at 0-indexed position i. If i equals the current length,
  the node is appended at the tail. If i is negative or greater than
  the current length, the operation is ignored (does nothing).
- "deleteAtIndex_i": delete the node at 0-indexed position i, if i is
  a valid index (0 <= i < length). Otherwise, ignore the operation.
- "get_i": look up the value of the node at 0-indexed position i.
  If i is not a valid index, the result is -1.

For example, the token "addAtIndex_2_9" means addAtIndex(index=2, val=9),
and "get_0" means get(index=0).

**Process every operation in `ops` in order, and return the list of results produced by every "get" operation, in the order they occurred.**

Operations that don't produce a result, like addAtHead, contribute nothing to the output.
constraints: -1000 <= index <= 1000 for any operation's index argument
notes: addAtIndex with index equal to the current length (append)
addAtIndex or deleteAtIndex with an out-of-range index (should be ignored)

sampleTestCases.explanation: the list starts empty, so index 0 is out of range

sampleTestCases.input: ops = "addAtHead_7 addAtHead_3 addAtHead_5 get_0 get_1 get_2 get_3"
sampleTestCases.explanation: after the three addAtHead calls the list is [5, 3, 7]; get_3 is out of range

sampleTestCases.input: ops = "addAtHead_1 addAtTail_3 addAtIndex_1_2 get_1 deleteAtIndex_0 get_0"
sampleTestCases.explanation: list becomes [1, 3], then addAtIndex_1_2 inserts 2 at position 1 giving [1, 2, 3]; get_1 = 2; deleteAtIndex_0 removes the 1, giving [2, 3]; get_0 = 2

optimal.time: O(n) per insert/delete operation with a real linked list once positioned, O(n) total array space
optimal.pattern: simulate with an actual linked list structure (or, for our array-returning representation, an array with careful index math), processing each token in order

bruteForce.approach: represent the list as a resizable array and implement each operation with array insert/remove at the given index (an O(n) shift per operation)
bruteForce.time: O(n) per operation, O(n^2) total in the worst case
